questions.learningObjective: Explain how the binder limits a day of work in egg tempera.

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: Because egg tempera dries almost at once in water, a passage cannot be adjusted once it has begun to set, so only a limited area can be painted and matched at a time. A marginal reminder adds: think about how quickly the binder sets. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: With “Explain how the binder limits a day of work in egg tempera. / Think about how quickly the binder sets. / Egg tempera and working…” settled, which choice remains consistent with the text?

answer.exemplar: Egg tempera binds with water and dries almost at once, so a stroke that is not placed within minutes will sit on a tacky, half-set film and tear the layer beneath it. The painter can therefore lay only a small passage at a time and must keep the day's painting matched to the dryness of what came before. The same quick set means each passage has to be judged and fixed while it is still workable.

questions.explanation: Because egg tempera dries almost at once in water, a passage cannot be adjusted once it has begun to set, so only a limited area can be painted and matched at a time. Long working sessions and the slow corrections possible in oil are unavailable.
questions.hint: Think about how quickly the binder sets.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why a canvas ground is built up in several thin layers.

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: A single thick layer would shrink unevenly and lift from the cloth, whereas thin dried layers keep the ground in contact with the support and spread the shrinkage. answer.exemplar: One thick layer applied to the cloth would shrink as it dried and would pull away from the weave in patches, because the cloth moves underneath it with changes in humidity. questions.hint: Think about how one thick layer would dry.

questions.learningObjective: Explain why a canvas painting must be stored rolled rather than folded.

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: Canvas expands and contracts with humidity, and a permanent fold concentrates that movement and adds stress the stiffer paint film cannot follow. A marginal reminder adds: think about the difference between a fold and a roll. It is followed by four candidate interpretations, of which exactly one is supported by the wording of the excerpt.

questions.stem: The question turns on what the note above shows about weave and paint film on canvas. Given the proposal "Think about the difference between a fold and a roll", which choice is consistent with the evidence in the passage?

answer.exemplar: Canvas moves with the changes in temperature and humidity of the store, expanding and contracting as it takes up and loses moisture, and a fold is a permanent set that cannot relax back out. A fold concentrates that movement at the crease and adds a stress that the paint film, which is stiffer than the cloth beneath it, cannot follow. Rolling distributes the strain around a wide cylinder instead, and the canvas can still relax when the conditions change.

questions.explanation: Canvas expands and contracts with humidity, and a permanent fold concentrates that movement and adds stress the stiffer paint film cannot follow. Rolling spreads the strain around a broad cylinder so the panel can still relax as conditions change.
questions.hint: Think about the difference between a fold and a roll.

answer.exemplar: In buon fresco the pigment is carried in water into a bed of wet lime, and it is locked in place by the carbonation of that lime as the wall dries. questions.learningObjective: Explain the hatched handling typical of egg tempera.

stimulus.body: Read this source excerpt carefully: Because a stroke cannot be blended into a passage that has already begun to set, tempera form is built from many small strokes laid beside and across one another. answer.exemplar: Egg tempera sets within minutes of being laid, so a brush stroke cannot be softened into the neighbouring passage after the first lines are down; it would drag and lift the half-set film rather than blend with it.
